intro: You are standing at the Bridge of Justinian, in Sakarya province, built in AD 559–562. Justinian threw this 430-metre bridge over the Sakarya. But look around you: the river later shifted its bed, and the bridge now stands largely on dry ground.
history: Justinian built the bridge between 559 and 562 to lift the road linking the capital to the eastern provinces above the floods of the Sakarya. Procopius, a contemporary witness, describes it. In later centuries the river shifted its bed, and so the 430-metre bridge now stands largely over dry ground.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the seven great arches and the remains of the triumphal arch, then the flood relief openings, and finally the northern abutment.
facts: Did you know? A triumphal arch once stood at one end. Its footings are still in place, and they show that the bridge was conceived as a monument, not merely a crossing. And the river later shifted its bed, which is why the 430-metre bridge now stands largely over dry ground.
outro: This brings our journey to the Bridge of Justinian to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The river may have moved on, but the bridge has stayed; let it stay for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
